subtitle: Words that belong together, and comparing at full stretch
words.intro: On a wet Sunday in the eleventh division, forty people and one dog watch a game. On Monday the local paper reports it in the language of a state funeral. A defeat is never just big. It’s *herb*, *bitter* or *empfindlich*.

grammar[0].fact: You can’t work these out, and your dictionary may not help. English has the same thing, of course: *heavy rain*, never *strong rain*. That’s why you should learn three words as one: *eine herbe Niederlage erleiden*.

grammar[1].blocks[0].title: one of the …: genitive plural
grammar[1].blocks[1].rows[0][1]: bei weitem · mit Abstand der beste
grammar[1].fact: After *einer der*, German needs a plural, in the genitive: *einer der besten Köche*. English has the same logic and the same trap in *one of the best cook*. With *mit Abstand*, you can then say how far ahead he is.

document.intro: A real ticket for the Vienna stadium, torn off by someone at the gate. Austria played England that May. Look at the small print: a whole contract in five lines, and a word this chapter has already taught you, *Rahmenprogramm*.
document.fact: Austria really did beat England that day, 3–1, in front of a huge crowd. An English paper might have called it a *bitter defeat*.
document.tasks[1].instruction: Complete each with the right verb.
reading.intro: Vroni’s paper is short of a sports reporter. Max has offered to cover FC Hofstraße II, because Jonas is in goal. They have lost nine–nil. Max has written his report in the best C2 German he knows, and Vroni is reading it out to the whole office. There is also a real sports editor, Herr Paschke, who has been doing this for 41 years.
reading.fact: Germany has many thousands of amateur clubs, and their games really are reported in local papers, often by a volunteer paid by the line. Words like *Moral* and *kämpferisch* are code: they mean the team lost. If the writer praises the *Rahmenprogramm*, the sausages were the best part.
reading.tasks[1].instruction: Say each thing the way a local paper would.
